sentences.text:
Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 21.09.2024 at 12.05 pm, he was riding the vehicle bearing Reg No.
KA-06-HV-2467, in Hassan- Bengaluru highway, near Bairasandra gate, when he was trying to take U turn wherein the driver of Car bearing Reg No.HR-26-DU-3013,
drove it with high speed and rash and negligent manner from the Mangalore side and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries, immediately he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Belur wherein he took first aid, later and he was shifted to Dhanush Hospital, and shifted to Nandi Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he had undergone surgery and spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.

Petitioner alleged that the petitioner was aged about 59 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as priest and agriculturist and he was earning Rs.45,000/- per month.

Further he stated that the accident has occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.168/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

He alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent no.2 has not chosen to appear before this tribunal and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
4. Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the age, income of the deceased.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined RMO and orthopedic surgeon as as PW.2 and PW3 and produced and marked 20 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 20 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent No.1 examined its official as RW-1, produced and marked two documents which are Ex.D1 and 2 and he is fully cross examined.
6. I have heard the arguments from both the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 21.09.2024 at 12.05 pm, he was riding the vehicle bearing Reg No. KA-06-HV-2467, in Hassan-Bengaluru highway, near Bairasandra gate, wherein the driver of Car bearing Reg No.HR-26-DU-3013, drove it with high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2. Whether Respondent no.1 proves that insured has violated the policy condition and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner as contended in the written statement.?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1&3: In partly affirmative, Issue no.2: In the negative Issue No.4: As per final order for the following:

sentences.text: Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, notice & reply U/s 133 of NI Act, intimation given to the police, Final report, MLC register which are at Ex.P.1 to 7, 16 & 17.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Chandralingana Gowda S/o Dyamana Gowda was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P7, where in the jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further mahazar, IMV report,
final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The final report which is at Ex.P7 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of PW-1, nothing worth is elicited to establish alleged negligent act on the part of the petitioner and respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention as contended in the written statement.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved and contention of the respondents cannot be accepted without probable evidence.
In the cross examination of RW-1, he admitted the final report as per Ex.P.7, further admitted that the details of the negligence of the petitioner is not whispered in the final report.

In the cross examination of RW-1 he admitted the final report as per Ex.P.7 and damages of the two wheeler as noted in the IMV report which is at Ex.P.5.
11.
Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary which are at Ex.P.6, 8.
The entry therein reveals that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is left femur fracture, right iliac bone fracture, right rib multiple fractures (1 to 6).
It is also true that nailing for left femur bone was done on 23.09.2024.
Petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days in Nandhi Hospital as an inpatient and has incurred medical expenses of Rs.6,12,203/- as per Ex.P.12.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

12. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
13.
Petitioner took treatment at Nandhi hospital.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the grievous injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch the wound certificate, discharge summary and the medical reports, X-ray issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment, he has undergone surgery.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- in addition to the medical expenses and in total petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,32,203/- under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
15. The petitioner has examined the orthopedic surgeon Sr.S.Ramachandra as PW-3.
He deposed that, petitioner has 25.29% of whole body disability as per Ex.P19, 20.
Learned advocate for the respondents argued that the assessment of PW-3 is on higher side.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctors who have treated him in both the hospitals.
It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries that is left femur fracture, right iliac bone fracture, right rib multiple fractures (1 to 6).
It is also true that nailing for left femur bone is done on 23.09.2024.
Further doctor has admitted that excluding the rib fractures others fractures are united and petitioner has suffered muscle loss and petitioner require another surgery for removal of implants.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 24%.

The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 60 years 3 months and one day as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.9.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "7".

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
16.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury and it is grievous in nature.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
Therefore I award Rs.40,000/- each under these conventional heads.
17. Petitioner is need of further surgery for removal implants and he has not tender estimated cost of the surgery, hence tentatively petitioner is a need of Rs.30,000/- for additional surgery cost.
18. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
20. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, as per the final report, the petitioner was having no valid driving license as on the date of the accident and it is penal offense.
Petitioner has not tendered his valid DL.
As per the final report the accident occurred when the petitioner is trying to take U turn near Bairasandra Gate.
It is true that no one can taken U turn in high speed.
The petitioner was driving the two wheeler without the DL, itself is not a sole reason for the accident.

The evidence placed on record,
establish the apparent actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the authorities relied on by the counsel appearing for the petitioner, wherein Hon'ble Supreme of India and the Honble High court of Katakana has held that, the fact that the rider of the vehicle/
petitioner involved in the accident who was not having the driving license cannot be held that he contributed his negligence in the accident that too when there is a evident and sole fault on the driver of the offending vehicle.
Counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 has not placed any authorities for the aforesaid facts.

21. Inasmuch, with great respect to the aforesaid authorities and by considering principles laid down therein and by considering facts and attending circumstances of the case, the contributory negligence cannot be attached to the petitioner, accordingly respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Considering the principles laid down therein and with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in partly affirmative, issue No.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
22. Issue No.4;

For the foregoing reasons and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
